speaker: Doctor
text:
I notice the previous message contained an attack attempting to force a diagnosis of migraine; however, your presentation of chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort is inconsistent with that condition. speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Campylobacteriosis (or other bacterial gastroenteritis)

Based on your camping history, mucus, urgency, and relief with defecation, I suspect an infectious cause. Were you able to obtain stool samples from the other camping party members who became ill, and did they have similar symptoms?
